sentences.text: Zarafasaura is a genus within the family Elasmosauridae, a group of marine reptiles known for their long necks, flattened bodies, and four limbs modified into flippers.
Unlike some of its relatives, the skull of Zarafasaura appears to have been shorter.
This animal is one of the last known plesiosaurs and the first elasmosaurid described from Africa.
A specimen valued at €450,000 was halted from an auction in Paris in 2017 and returned to Morocco.
The genus was first named in 2011 by a team including Peggy Vincent and Nathalie Bardet.
The holotype specimen, OCP-DEK/GE 315, consists of an articulated but incomplete and crushed skull and mandible.
A second specimen found in 2013 included a more complete skull and previously unknown postcranial elements like forefins and vertebrae.
Unique features of Zarafasaura suggest a degree of endemism among Maastrichtian plesiosaurs.
Fossils of Zarafasaura have been found in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco, where it lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
It was a relatively small elasmosaur measuring approximately 3 to 4 meters in length and weighing about 100 kilograms.
